rationale: I read the held FR text of 10 FR 4253 and the held text of EO 9643 (10 FR 13039). Identity: EO 9541 signed April 19, 1945 transfers the Office of Surplus Property of Treasury's Procurement Division to Commerce, effective May 1, 1945, matching the API observation (the editorial note 'See: EO 9643, October 19, 1945') and the 1989 row 'Office terminated by EO 9643'. Sections 1 and 2 are one-time transfers of the office, records, property, funds and personnel, performed at the May 1, 1945 effective date, but the text does not itself say they were completed. Section 3 is a continuing authorization for the two departments to supply each other materials and services 'for such period after the effective date as may be mutually agreeable'. EO 9643 (ACTOR_TEXT:EO:9643) says the Office of Surplus Property in the Department of Commerce is terminated effective November 5, 1945 and transfers its functions to the RFC. It does not mention EO 9541, does not revoke or supersede it, and does not address section 3; it terminates the office EO 9541 had placed in Commerce, which is a lead that the transferred subject matter ended, not an express end of all of EO 9541's commands. The 1989 note is a lead only. cruden.py number EO:9541 found 0 held instruments citing it. A NO would require inferring that section 3 lapsed with the office, which no held text says, so I leave it unrecommended; an independent reviewer may reasonably read performance of secs. 1-2 plus the office's termination as ending the order, but that is not shown by the held text.
